transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

My mom made me come. She keeps asking what's wrong, but I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room all day with the exact same clothes on. It's this shirt, actually. I got it at a thrift store with my friend Becca before she moved away to Florida. Florida has way too many bugs, I saw this documentary about these huge palmetto bugs they have down there and it made my skin crawl just thinking about them getting into the house. They can fly, too, which is just wrong for a bug that big. But yeah, I don't knit or write in my journal or go walking like I used to. I just sit there. I have all this blue yarn for a scarf sitting right next to my bed but I just... can't.
How long have you been feeling this way, where it's hard to find the energy to do anything?

I guess... well, this whole decline, it’s been going on since I started the community-college program. That was about two years and two months ago. I was supposed to take this art history class because the textbook had a really pretty painting on it, this woman holding a parasol. Parasols are kind of making a comeback, I think. I saw a girl walking down the street with a black lace one last summer, but it wasn't even sunny out. It was actually drizzling. Rain ruins lace so fast, especially if it's vintage, you know? You have to hand wash it in the sink with that special gentle soap. But the soap smells like lavender, and lavender always reminds me of my grandma's guest bathroom. She had these little soaps shaped like seashells sitting in a glass dish that you weren't allowed to actually use, they were just for looking at. I never understood the point of soap you can't wash your hands with.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or whispering that other people around you couldn't hear?

Um, no, not that I've noticed. I mean, I hear people whispering sometimes, but that's just regular people actually whispering. Like when I used to go to the library. The librarian there was always shushing everyone, but she had this really loud shush, which is kind of ironic, you know? She wore these reading glasses on a little gold chain around her neck. My aunt had a chain exactly like that for her sunglasses, but she lost them at the beach a few years ago. The sand just gets absolutely everywhere when you go to the beach. It sticks to your sunscreen and then you bring it all back into the car on your towels. I hate vacuuming the car, the cord for the vacuum never reaches far enough from the garage outlet. We used to have this really long orange extension cord but my dad ran over it with the lawnmower. It made this awful crunching sound. But... yeah, no, I don't hear any voices or sounds that aren't really there.
{"intent": "Screen for manic or hypomanic episodes to evaluate for bipolar disorder", "question": "Have there ever been times when you felt the complete opposite—unusually

Unusually what? Like, energetic or happy? Um, no. I've never really felt like that. I'm pretty much always just tired. Even if I try to drink an energy drink, it doesn't do anything. My brother used to drink those Monster drinks all the time when he would stay up playing video games. He built this massive pyramid of empty green cans on his desk. It fell over once in the middle of the night and sounded exactly like a car crash. Car crashes are so scary. I saw one on the highway once where the bumper was completely ripped off and just lying in the ditch. The grass in those ditches is always so long and dead-looking. They really should mow it more often, but I guess it's probably dangerous for the workers with all the semi-trucks speeding by. The trucks always make my car shake when they pass. But... yeah, no, I don't get bursts of energy or anything like that.
Have you ever felt like people were watching you, talking about you behind your back, or trying to harm you?

Well, yeah, I do know they talk about me. I mean, since I was in those community college classes, I've just known. The people running the school portal and the clinic practicum, they use these little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me. They do it so everyone knows I'm someone they don't want in healthcare. My mom says they're just regular messages, but she doesn't read them the way I do. She reads her emails on her phone, and the screen is so small. I don't know how she sees anything. She has this cracked screen protector that she refuses to replace, and it has a bubble right in the middle. Bubbles in screen protectors are so annoying. It's like when you're putting up wallpaper and you get an air pocket, and you have to use that little plastic squeegee thing to push it out to the edge. My dad put up wallpaper in the hallway when I was little, and it had a pattern of little sailboats. Sailboats always look so peaceful, but I bet being on one is actually really loud with the wind and the sails flapping. The fabric on sails is really heavy, kind of like canvas. You could probably make a really sturdy tote bag out of an old sail. I need a new tote bag for my groceries, the paper ones always rip at the bottom if you buy anything heavy, like a jar of pickles. Pickles are so good, especially the spicy garlic ones. But yeah, the school portal people are definitely trying to push me out.
Aside from having low energy, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless?

Um, no, not really sad or anything. Just... tired. Like I said, the energy just isn't there. It feels like when you leave your phone off the charger overnight and you wake up and it's at like, two percent. And then you have to find the cord, but the cord is always tangled up with something else. I have this drawer in my room that's just full of tangled cords. There's an old charger in there for a flip phone I had in middle school. It was pink and it had little rhinestones stuck to it, but half of them fell off. I tried to glue them back on with superglue once, but I got the glue on my fingers and they stuck together. Superglue is so dangerous, honestly. You have to use nail polish remover to get it off. The smell of nail polish remover always gives me a headache. It's so strong, kind of like the smell of sharpies. I love writing with sharpies, though, the way they glide on paper is really satisfying. You have to be careful not to let them bleed through to the next page, especially in a notebook. Notebooks with thin paper are the worst. But... no, I don't feel sad or hopeless. Just really, really tired.

```json
{
  "intent": "Check for first-rank symptoms of schizophrenia, specifically thought broadcasting, insertion, or withdrawal, to differentiate schizophrenia from delusional disorder.",
  "question":

"Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being broadcast so others could hear them, or like thoughts were being put into your head or taken away?"

Um, no? I don't... I don't think so. My thoughts are just my thoughts, you know? They stay in my head. Sometimes my head hurts if I think too much, like when I was trying to figure out how to fix my headphones. The left side stopped working, and it's so annoying when you can only hear music in one ear. It makes the song sound completely different. I was listening to this one song by that band with the lead singer who always wears the big hats... I can't remember their name right now. But hats are making a comeback, I think. I saw a girl at the grocery store wearing a huge sun hat in the middle of winter. It was kind of weird, but also kind of cool. Maybe she was going on vacation somewhere warm. I'd love to go to the beach, the sand always feels so nice between your toes. But then it gets everywhere in your car, and vacuuming the car is such a chore. The vacuum at the car wash never has enough suction. It's like trying to suck up dirt with a straw. But, um, no, no one is putting thoughts in my head or taking them out. That sounds like a sci-fi movie or something.
Have you used any substances, like marijuana, alcohol, or other drugs, during this time?

Um, no, I don't really do any of that stuff. No drugs or drinking. I mean, my brother used to smoke a lot of weed when he was in high school, and it always made his room smell terrible. It's like this skunky, sweet smell that just gets stuck in the carpet. Carpet is so hard to keep clean anyway. We had this white carpet in our old house, which was a terrible idea because someone spilled cranberry juice on it on Thanksgiving. Cranberry juice stains are impossible to get out. You have to blot it, not rub it, but my aunt rubbed it and it just spread into this huge pink blob. Pink is a nice color, though. I had a pink bicycle when I was little, with streamers on the handlebars. I loved riding it down the big hill in our neighborhood, even though the brakes squeaked really loud. Squeaky brakes are so dangerous, you really have to get those checked. But yeah, no, I don't use any substances or anything. Just... not my thing.

  "intent": "Assess for bodily or somatic hallucinations to differentiate between schizophrenia subtypes and delusional disorder.",
  "question": "Have you ever felt unusual or unexplained sensations inside your

Um, unusual sensations? Inside my body? No, I haven't really felt anything weird like that. I mean, sometimes my stomach rumbles really loud when I'm hungry, like it's its own person. It happened during a test in high school once, during finals week, and it was so quiet in the room that everyone heard it. It was so embarrassing. Finals week was always the worst, anyway. I had this one history teacher who made us memorize all these dates for the Civil War, and I can never remember dates. I can't even remember my own cousin's birthday half the time. I think it's in October? Or maybe November. November is a weird month because it's right before Christmas, but it's not quite winter yet, so you never know what kind of jacket to wear. I have this really nice denim jacket, but the buttons are kind of loose. I need to sew them back on, but threading a needle is so frustrating. The thread always frays at the end. But, um... no, no strange feelings inside my body or anything. Just the normal stuff.

```json
{
  "intent": "Assess for catatonic symptoms such as posturing or motor immobility to differentiate undifferentiated schizophrenia from paranoid schizophrenia.",
  "question": "Have you

Have I... like, frozen like a statue or something? Um, no, I don't think I do that. I move around fine. I mean, unless I'm playing freeze tag, but I haven't played that since elementary school. We used to play it on the blacktop out back, and if you fell, you'd scrape your knees so bad. The school nurse always had those really stiff, cheap band-aids that never actually stuck to your skin. They'd just peel off the second you started sweating. Sweating is so gross anyway. Summer is my least favorite season because it's just too hot, and the mosquitoes are absolutely everywhere. I got a mosquito bite right on my ankle last year and I scratched it so much it left a little scar. Scars are kind of weird, right? How the skin just heals back completely different. Like it remembers what happened. I wonder if trees get scars when you carve your initials into them. People always do that at the park near my house, just carving hearts and letters into the bark with pocket knives. It seems kind of mean to the tree, honestly, like they didn't ask for a tattoo. But yeah, no, I don't get stuck in weird positions or freeze up or anything like that.

```json
{
  "intent": "Rule out general medical conditions or neurological causes for these symptoms.",
  "question": "Have you ever had any major medical problems, head injuries, or

Um, head injuries? Or like big medical problems? No, I've never really been in the hospital for anything serious. I mean, I broke my arm once when I was seven, falling off the monkey bars. The monkey bars at that park were super rusty, though, so it was probably an accident waiting to happen. Rust is so weird, how it just eats away at metal like that. My dad had this old truck that was basically more rust than truck by the time he finally sold it. It was this ugly mustard yellow color. Yellow is such a hard color to pull off, unless you're a sunflower, I guess. Sunflowers are my favorite. They get so tall, sometimes taller than a person, which is kind of intimidating if you think about it. Like a giant flower just staring down at you. I tried to grow some in a pot on my windowsill once, but they died pretty much immediately. I don't have a green thumb at all. I can't even keep a cactus alive, and those are supposed to be foolproof. But yeah, no head injuries or anything like that. Just the broken arm a long time ago.

```json

  "intent": "Assess for visual hallucinations to complete the evaluation for perceptual disturbances.",
  "question": "Have you ever seen things, like

Seen things? Like, things that aren't actually there? Um, no, I haven't seen anything like that. My vision is actually pretty good, I think. I haven't been to the eye doctor since I was in middle school, though. We went to this place in the mall, right next to that pretzel stand. Oh my gosh, the smell of those pretzels is so good. I always get the cinnamon sugar ones, but they put way too much sugar in the little paper bag and it gets all over your fingers. And then if you touch your clothes, you just have sticky sugar everywhere. My mom used to get so mad if I ate them in her car. She keeps her car spotless, like, she vacuums the floor mats every single Sunday morning. I don't really get why people care so much about cars, honestly. Like, it's just a machine to get you to the grocery store or whatever. I don't drive anyway, parallel parking just seems completely impossible to figure out. How do you even know where the back of the bumper is? But, yeah... no, I don't see any weird things or anything like that.

  "question": "Have people ever mentioned that your facial expressions seem blank

Blank? Like I'm not smiling or whatever? I don't know, maybe. Mostly I just... I can't really make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room. I wear the same clothes, like, I haven't changed this sweater in a few days. It's really soft, though. I got it at a thrift store. Thrift stores always smell kind of dusty, like old books and mothballs. I used to love looking for vintage buttons there for my knitting. I don't knit anymore, though. Or journal, or go for walks. I used to walk down by the creek, but the water always looks so muddy after it rains. Mud is just dirt and water, but it stains so badly. My mom gets so frustrated when I don't do anything, she'll come in and ask what's wrong, and I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. It's like my voice is too heavy to use. Heavy things are so hard to move. Like pianos. How do people even move pianos when they buy a new house? They must have special dollies or something. But yeah, I don't know about my face being blank, I just don't have the energy to do much of anything.

  "intent": "Assess for inappropriate affect to determine if criteria for disorganized schizophrenia are met.",

Laughing? Like, when I'm not supposed to? I don't really know. I don't think I laugh much at all lately. Laughing takes a lot of energy, honestly. It's like you have to use all these muscles in your face and stomach. Speaking of stomachs, I tried to eat some soup earlier, but it was just... too hot. It was tomato soup. Tomato soup is always better with grilled cheese, but making a sandwich is just too much work right now. You have to get the butter perfectly soft so it doesn't tear the bread. Tearing bread is the worst, especially when it's that really soft white bread. My grandma used to make her own bread from scratch. She had this huge wooden bowl she used just for kneading the dough. Wood is such a nice material, it feels so warm compared to plastic or metal. I wish more things were made of wood these days. Everything is just plastic now, and it breaks so easily. Like those plastic hangers in my closet, they just snap if you pull a shirt off too fast. But um, no, I don't really find myself laughing. I just sit there mostly.
{"intent": "Assess for aimless, silly, or irresponsible behavior to evaluate criteria for hebephrenic schizophrenia", "question": "Have you found yourself acting silly, playing pranks,

Playing pranks? Silly? Um, no. I don't really do anything like that. I don't really do anything at all, to be honest. I just stay in my room. My room has these really big windows, which is nice, I guess. But the curtains are always closed. They're these heavy, dark blue curtains. Blue is supposed to be a calming color, right? Like the ocean. I went to the ocean once when I was little. The sand got everywhere, in my shoes, in the car. It's so hard to vacuum sand out of a car. Car vacuums never have enough suction. You really need one of those big shop vacs, the ones that are shaped like a barrel. My dad had one in his garage. He was always building things out of wood. Woodworking seems so complicated, with all the different saws and sanders. Sawdust smells really good, though. Like pine trees. But yeah, no, I don't play pranks or act silly. I just don't have the energy for it.

  "intent": "Assess for hallucinations of smell or taste to evaluate criteria for paranoid schizophrenia.",
  "question": "Have you noticed any strange or unusual

Strange or unusual... smells? Or tastes? No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. Everything just tastes kind of bland lately, honestly. Like cardboard. Cardboard boxes are so useful for moving, but they take up so much space when you break them down. We have a whole stack of them in the garage from when my sister moved out. She moved to Chicago. Chicago is supposed to be really windy. The "Windy City." I wonder if it's actually windier there than other places, or if it's just a nickname. Nicknames are weird. My uncle used to call me "Bug" when I was little, because I was always crawling around looking at insects. Ladybugs are my favorite. They're supposed to be good luck if they land on you. But I haven't seen a ladybug in a really long time. I don't really go outside much anymore to see them. So, no, no weird smells or anything. Just... bland.

```json

  "intent": "Assess for delusions of control or passivity to evaluate first-rank symptoms of schizophrenia.",
  "question": "Have you ever felt

Felt like... like someone else was making me do things? Or controlling me? No, I don't think so. I mean, my mom tries to tell me what to do all the time. She always wants me to clean my room or come downstairs for dinner. Dinner is usually around six, but sometimes it's later if she has to work late. She works at a bank. Banks are always so quiet, you know? Like you're not supposed to talk above a whisper. It's like being in a library. I used to go to the library all the time when I was in high school. They had this really great section on astronomy. I loved looking at the pictures of the galaxies and nebulas. The colors are so bright, pinks and purples and blues. It's crazy to think about how big the universe is, and how small we are. Like little ants just crawling around. But no, I don't feel like anyone is controlling my thoughts or my body or anything like that. Just my mom being bossy, I guess.

  "intent": "Assess for delusions of jealousy to evaluate criteria for paranoid schizophrenia or delusional disorder.",
  "question": "Have you had strong

Strong... like, strong feelings about someone? Or being jealous? Um, no, I don't really have anything like that. I don't even have a boyfriend or anyone to be jealous about anyway. I haven't really dated since high school. High school feels like it was forever ago, even though it wasn't. We had this big clock in the hallway that was always five minutes fast. Everyone knew it was fast, but the principal refused to fix it because he said it kept people from being late. Being late is the worst feeling, like your stomach drops. I used to get that feeling on the bus. The bus always smelled like wet rubber and exhaust. Exhaust fumes are so bad for the environment, you know? All those cars just pumping out smog. I read an article about how the smog in some cities is so thick you can't even see the buildings. Buildings in big cities are made of so much glass now. I wonder who cleans all those windows. It must be a terrifying job, hanging from a little platform way up in the sky. I don't like heights very much. But yeah, no, I don't have any strong jealous feelings or anything like that. Just me here in my room.

```json
{
  "intent": "Assess for grandiose delusions to further evaluate the delusional profile for paranoid schizophrenia.",
  "question": "Have you ever felt like you have special abilities, powers

Powers? Like... special abilities? No, I don't have anything like that. I can't read minds or fly or anything crazy. Flying would be way too cold anyway. You know how high up airplanes go? The air outside them is freezing. I went on an airplane once when I was little to see my grandma in Florida. Florida is so humid, it makes your hair frizz up like a giant puffball. My mom used to try and brush my hair out when it got like that, but it just made it worse. She used this pink plastic brush that had little beads on the end of the bristles, but half the beads had fallen off so it just scratched my scalp. I hate getting scratched. It reminds me of my neighbor's cat, Barnaby. He looks really fluffy but he's actually super mean if you try to pet his stomach. Cats are so unpredictable, you know? One second they're purring, and the next they're biting your hand. I prefer dogs, they're just happy all the time and they wag their tails. But yeah, no special powers or anything for me. Just normal.

Blank? Like, just stopping? Um, no, I don't think my thoughts ever just stop. They're usually going pretty fast, actually. Sometimes it's like a radio that's stuck between stations, you know? Just a lot of static and talking. I used to listen to the radio all the time in my dad's truck. He had this old Ford, it was painted this really ugly shade of green, like pea soup. I hate pea soup. My grandma used to make it every Thanksgiving, and she'd always try to force me to eat it. Thanksgiving is always so stressful anyway, with all the relatives asking you what you're doing with your life. I just graduated high school, I don't know what I'm doing yet! It's too much pressure. Pressure makes diamonds, they say, but I think it just makes people crack. Like an egg. Have you ever tried to balance an egg on its end? We did that in science class once. You're supposed to be able to do it on the vernal equinox, but I think that's a myth. Myths are interesting, though. Like the Greek gods, they were always messing with people. But no, my thoughts don't go blank. They just keep going.
